sessionTitle: Expand local AI reach with Windows ML

announcements.name: Windows ML CLI (new tool)
announcements.shortDescription: A new command-line tool for converting and optimizing models to run locally on Windows across CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs, including `hub`, `export`, and optimization commands.
announcements.longDescription: The Windows ML CLI is a new command-line tool that helps developers convert and optimize models to run locally on Windows across CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs. It was highlighted as part of what's new with Windows ML in 2026.

announcements.name: Windows ML 2.0
announcements.shortDescription: Updated to bring ONNX Runtime 1.24 with performance and stability improvements plus newly updated plugin-based execution providers usable across different runtime versions.
announcements.longDescription: Windows ML has been updated to version 2.0, bringing ONNX Runtime 1.24, which includes a number of performance and stability updates. It also adds newly updated plugin-based execution providers that have performance improvements and allow execution providers to be used across different runtime versions more easily.

announcements.name: WebNN now backed by Windows ML
announcements.shortDescription: On Windows, WebNN uses Windows ML for faster hardware-accelerated inferencing in Edge or Chrome browsers (currently in developer preview).
announcements.longDescription: WebNN is being updated to use Windows ML when running on Windows, as demonstrated earlier in the session. This leads to faster hardware-accelerated machine learning model inferencing when using the Edge or Chrome browsers.

announcements.name: ORT Gen AI library performance updates
announcements.shortDescription: The Windows ML ORT Gen AI library received updates leading to faster local LLM inferencing on Windows.
announcements.longDescription: The Windows ML ORT Gen AI library has received a number of performance updates, leading to faster local LLM inferencing on Windows.

announcements.name: Dynamic execution provider acquisition
announcements.shortDescription: Apps can dynamically acquire vendor execution providers (e.g. QNN) via Windows Update rather than bundling roughly 80 MB of providers, reducing app size.
announcements.longDescription: Windows ML allows apps to dynamically acquire hardware vendor execution providers (SDKs built by vendors like AMD, Intel, NVIDIA, and Qualcomm that accelerate models on NPUs, GPUs, and CPUs) rather than bundling them. This means an app doesn't need to carry roughly 80 MB of providers, reducing app size and simplifying distribution. In the demo, the app creates an ORT environment, uses the Find All Providers API to discover compatible execution providers, locates the QNN EP, calls EnsureReadyAsync to make it ready, and registers it to the environment.
